requirement_checks.criterion: Application-level definition and execution of multiple containers.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: Helm explicitly defines, installs and upgrades applications with many interdependent parts. Charts package related application manifests and dependencies into one installed release; the docs use WordPress plus MySQL and distinguish application operation from cluster operation. This establishes multi-container application declaration and execution through a pre-existing Kubernetes cluster.

requirement_checks.criterion: Explicit Docker interface.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: The documented client and library communicate with the Kubernetes API server. Docker image references in the usage guide establish image inputs, not an explicit Docker engine or Docker-facing execution interface.

requirement_checks.criterion: Container-based system assembly contributes runtime foundation; cluster operators, monitoring and VM wrappers are different functions.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: Charts assemble related application resources and dependencies for installation together. This is application system assembly on an existing runtime foundation; the docs explicitly put operating the cluster itself outside Helm scope.

requirement_checks.criterion: Application-level definition and execution of multiple containers.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: The official application tutorial supplies one YAML definition containing foo and bar container Pods, their Services and a shared Ingress, then applies it and verifies both routes. minikube provides or downloads kubectl and hosts the declared application. This exact-project example establishes definition and execution of multiple application containers, rather than merely assuming upstream capability.

requirement_checks.criterion: Explicit Docker interface.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: The start guide explicitly supports a Docker container environment and documents Docker Desktop ingress access through minikube tunnel. This Docker-backed cluster interface is distinct from an application-level Docker Compose interface, which was not established.

requirement_checks.criterion: Container-based system assembly contributes runtime foundation; cluster operators, monitoring and VM wrappers are different functions.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: The Docker-backed route creates local Kubernetes and provides kubectl, networking, application services and ingress for the demonstrated container workloads. This contributes a container runtime foundation; VM drivers are alternative routes and do not alone establish this contribution.

requirement_checks.criterion: Application-level definition and execution of multiple containers.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: K3s explicitly supports configurable application chart templates, bundles a controller that installs and reconfigures those charts, and auto-deploys manifest files. The repository additionally states automatic deployment of Kubernetes resources from local manifests. This provides an exact-project application declaration/execution interface for related chart resources, rather than relying on the lightweight Kubernetes label alone.

requirement_checks.criterion: Explicit Docker interface.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: The official Docker-runtime section documents the --docker option, embedded cri-dockerd communication with dockerd, and verification with docker ps. This is an explicit Docker runtime integration, not an inference from Dockerfiles; the application declaration remains Kubernetes manifests.

requirement_checks.criterion: Container-based system assembly contributes runtime foundation; cluster operators, monitoring and VM wrappers are different functions.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: The distribution explicitly bundles containerd/runc, networking, DNS, ingress, load balancing, volumes and manifest deployment into one cohesive runtime. This assembles the container-based application foundation rather than only monitoring or exposing cluster-management commands.

requirement_checks.criterion: Application-level definition and execution of multiple containers.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: The guide loads my-app, my-db and my-cache images and documents kubectl apply for an application manifest. It establishes an application deployment workflow requiring separate kubectl, but does not show a combined multi-container application definition or its execution in the inspected example. Cluster creation and loading several images alone do not confirm the complete core; unrelatedness is not established.

requirement_checks.criterion: Explicit Docker interface.
requirement_checks.concise_rationale: The guide explicitly selects Docker as the node provider, exposes kind load docker-image, and inspects nodes using docker exec. These are direct Docker interfaces for cluster and image preparation; an application-level Docker Compose interface is unestablished.

requirement_checks.criterion: Container-based system assembly contributes runtime foundation; cluster operators, monitoring and VM wrappers are different functions.

requirement_checks.criterion: Application-level definition and execution of multiple containers.

requirement_checks.criterion: Container-based system assembly contributes runtime foundation; cluster operators, monitoring and VM wrappers are different functions.

requirement_checks.criterion: Application-level definition and execution of multiple containers.
